messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each city with appropriate facilities. The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

We need to pass an array for Cafe? Actually the type says "Cafe"[] meaning an array of strings? But the enumeration includes "Cafe"[], so maybe we pass ["Cafe"]? The function expects a single value from the union, but "Cafe"[] is an array type. So we need to pass an array of strings? The type is ambiguous. But likely we need to pass an array of strings for Cafe. For example, facilities: ["Cafe"].

Thus for each city:

NYC: Reading Room and Fiction. So facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

LA: Wi-Fi and Children Section. So facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

Chicago: Cafe and Reading Room. So facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to call the function three times. Use the function calls.
